chunks.text: About Escoffier · AIchef.food The chef behind our chef About Auguste Escoffier (1846–1935) The French chef who organised the modern professional kitchen and wrote down the classic repertoire. His book still shapes how chefs cook today, and it grounds every recipe on this site. His life Born in 1846 in Villeneuve-Loubet, near Nice. He was apprenticed in his uncle’s restaurant in Nice at the age of 12. Worked with the hotelier César Ritz: Monte Carlo, then the Savoy in London (from 1890), the Ritz in Paris (1898) and the Carlton in London (1899–1920). Made a Chevalier of the Légion d’honneur in 1919 and promoted to Officier in 1928.

chunks.title: About Escoffier · AIchef.food
chunks.text: In 1928 he also became the first president of the World Association of Chefs’ Societies. Died in Monte Carlo in 1935, aged 88. His work Brigade de cuisine: drawing on his years as an army chef, he organised the kitchen into stations (sauces, fish, roasts, vegetables, pastry), each run by a chef de partie . This made service faster, cleaner and more consistent. Five mother sauces: building on Carême’s system, he set out béchamel, velouté, espagnole, tomato and hollandaise as the foundations from which other sauces are made. Service à la russe: he championed serving courses one after another, as the dishes are listed on the menu. Le Guide Culinaire (1903).

chunks.title: About Escoffier · AIchef.food
chunks.text: The 1907 English translation, A Guide to Modern Cookery , has 2,999 numbered recipes and is our Classics library. Created dishes such as Pêche Melba and Melba toast , named after the Australian soprano Nellie Melba. His cuisine Simplicity: he cut back on heavy garnish and show, and let the main ingredient lead. Foundations: good stocks ( fonds ), glazes and mother sauces come first. Balance: lighter sauces and restraint, so that flavours stay in harmony. Seasonality: menus built around what was best at market. “King of chefs and chef of kings” Escoffier is widely called le roi des cuisiniers et le cuisinier des rois . The French press used the phrase for him, as it had earlier for Carême.

chunks.title: About Escoffier · AIchef.food
chunks.text: A popular story also has Kaiser Wilhelm II calling him the “emperor of chefs” in 1913, but that is legend rather than a documented quotation. Many chefs and food historians rank him among the most influential cooks of all time: the brigade system and the classic sauce repertoire are still taught in professional kitchens. “The greatest of all time” is an honorific and a widely held view, not a measurable fact. How Escoffier shapes Malcolm AI Chef Grounded answers: for each search, we look up the most relevant entries in the 1907 Guide (and the stocks and sauces they rely on) and give them to Malcolm as reference material.

chunks.text: Dioscorides & Medicinal cuisine · AIchef.food The physician behind Medicinal cuisine Pedanius Dioscorides (c. 40–90 AD) A Greek physician from Cilicia whose De Materia Medica described around six hundred plants and a thousand preparations. For some 1,500 years it was the reference on herbs, foods and their virtues, and it now grounds Malcolm’s Medicinal cuisine. Historical, not medical. The uses below are what Dioscorides recorded nearly 2,000 years ago, shared for culinary and cultural interest. They are not medical advice, and no dish here treats, cures or prevents any illness.

chunks.title: Dioscorides & Medicinal cuisine · AIchef.food
chunks.text: If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, on medication or have a health condition, speak to a doctor or pharmacist before using herbs in quantity. His life Born at Anazarbus (Anazarbos) in Cilicia, near Tarsus in modern Turkey, then part of the Roman Empire. Lived about 40–90 AD, under the emperors Nero and Vespasian . Practised as an army doctor with the Roman legions in Greece, Italy, Asia Minor and Provence, collecting and testing plants as he travelled. He wrote his herbal around 64 AD, at the suggestion of his fellow physician Areius, and may have used the library at Alexandria.

chunks.title: Dioscorides & Medicinal cuisine · AIchef.food
chunks.text: His work De Materia Medica (“On medical material”) has five books: aromatics, oils and trees; living creatures, cereals and vegetables; roots; other herbs; then vines, wines and minerals. It describes each plant’s appearance and where it grows, then how to prepare it and what it was used for. That practical focus made it unusually useful. Food sits at its heart: barley water, honey and oxymel, olive oils, lentils, cabbage, garlic, fennel, figs, quinces and wines. His legacy It was copied for centuries. The illuminated Vienna Dioscorides (Codex Vindobonensis, c. 512 AD) was made for Princess Juliana Anicia.

chunks.title: Dioscorides & Medicinal cuisine · AIchef.food
chunks.text: Latin editions were printed from 1478, and Aldus Manutius printed the Greek text in Venice in 1499. Mattioli’s commentaries (1544 onwards) spread it across Renaissance Europe. John Goodyer translated it into English in 1655. It shaped European pharmacy and botany into the 17th century. How Malcolm cooks “Medicinal” Tick Medicinal under Cuisines (on its own, or fused with others such as Moroccan), or choose the Dioscorides Inspiration mode.
